newsitem.title: JAPAN: Indonesia raises LPG allotment to Japan--traders.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia raises LPG allotment to Japan--traders.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned oil concern Pertamina has revised up its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) allocation to Japan by 120,000 tonnes to 1.66 million tonnes for 1997, LPG traders said on Monday.

Pertamina has raised term LPG volume to be lifted at Bontang to one million tonnes, up by 200,000 tonnes from the original allotment, while cutting term cargoes to be loaded at Arun by 80,000 tonnes to 660,000 tonnes, they said.
The term price will be rolled over from 1996 at Saudi Arabia's contract price (CP) plus $12 per tonne on a free on board (FOB) basis, traders said.
Indonesia allocated about two million tonnes of term LPG cargoes to Japan for 1996, they added.
